title: Best Gaming & VR Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare four VPNs for gaming and VR privacy on one published rubric, including what a VPN can and can't protect from gaming platforms and headsets.
intro: Gaming platforms and VR headsets collect large amounts of personal data, from biometric information to voice recordings. This page scores four VPNs on the same criteria. A VPN hides your IP address and encrypts your traffic, but it can't stop a headset or gaming platform collecting data about you.

verdict.summary: On these five criteria Mullvad VPN, NordVPN and Surfshark VPN tie for the top score; Mullvad VPN is listed first only because ties are ordered alphabetically. ExpressVPN is a little lower because its tracker blocker is only on the Advanced and Pro plans. All four hide your IP address from other players and encrypt your traffic on the network, but none can stop a headset or gaming platform from collecting data about you; use the platform's own privacy settings for that. Latency isn't scored: it depends mostly on how far the VPN server is from you and from the game server, and we haven't measured it.

pro_tips: Always enable VPN before launching gaming clients to encrypt all data from the start of your session.
Use a browser that blocks third-party trackers when researching games, reading forums, or shopping on gaming marketplaces.
Configure your VPN on your router to protect gaming consoles that don't support VPN apps directly.
Regularly review and adjust privacy settings on gaming platforms like Steam, Xbox Live, and PlayStation Network.
Consider using separate email addresses for gaming accounts to compartmentalize your digital identity.

faqs.question: Will a VPN slow down my gaming performance?
faqs.answer: A VPN adds some delay because your traffic takes an extra hop. How much depends mostly on how far the VPN server is from you and from the game server, so choose servers close to both for minimal impact.

faqs.question: Do VPNs protect my data in VR games?
faqs.answer: Only in transit. A VPN encrypts the traffic between your headset and the VPN server, which hides it from your local network and ISP, but the data still reaches the platform in full. It can't stop the headset or the platform from collecting biometric, movement or voice data; use the headset's privacy settings for that.

faqs.question: Can I use a VPN on gaming consoles?
faqs.answer: Most consoles don't support VPN apps directly, but you can configure your router with VPN or use connection sharing from a VPN-enabled computer to protect console gaming.

faqs.question: Are free VPNs safe for gaming?
faqs.answer: Free VPNs often log user data, have slow speeds, and limited server options. For gaming privacy, invest in a reputable paid VPN service with strong privacy policies.

faqs.question: How do I check if my gaming VPN is working?
faqs.answer: Use IP checking websites before and after connecting to VPN, and verify your location appears different. Also check for DNS leaks using online tools to ensure complete protection.
